what_happened.line: The Finance and School Committees met jointly and heard a Chapter 70 explainer covering the foundation budget, the required local contribution, circuit breaker and Monty Tech assessments.
The explainer said Chapter 70 foundation aid is less than last year's, so hold harmless and a minimum per-pupil increase make up the difference.
The Finance Committee agreed that the November 4 public hearing will take the TC Passios articles in one combined presentation, with discussion able to cross articles.
The committee set the December 9 agenda: a Chapter 70 follow-up with legislators, ARPA, and Green Communities and streetlights.
Committee reports raised a master plan funding request and a dispute with the utility over the quoted streetlight purchase cost, which the DPU may be asked to settle.

why_it_matters: Chapter 70 state aid is a large share of the school appropriation, and the minimum increase and hold harmless rules set how much of the school budget the town's tax levy has to cover.
The November 4 hearing on the TC Passios articles comes before a special town meeting on November 16, where residents may be asked to vote on those articles.
watch_next: November 4 public hearing on the TC Passios articles, ahead of the November 16 special town meeting.
December 9 Finance Committee meeting: Chapter 70 follow-up with legislators, ARPA, and Green Communities/streetlights.
